head: 31ca678e88cb536e694ff513b1b623f387ca17fe
classification_reasons: The spec is tight now (every flagged concern closed with an explicit decision, and the one gap this re-review was asked to check -- the duplicate-glob-match fail case missing from plan.md's test enumerations -- is now closed everywhere it needed to be), but blast radius is not small: a brand-new module (plugin/lessons/index.py), a new gate check registered in CHECKS_BY_PHASE['e'], edits to two command files' allowed-tools and instructions, two template files, OPERATING_MODEL.md and a two-manifest version bump, with plan.md's own Risk 2 still naming the gate check as the step whose failure mode would silently stop enforcing the invariant rather than failing loudly.

None of the touched behavior is covered by any existing test: plugin/lessons/index.py and lesson_and_eval are new; every test proving them (test_lessons.py, the new test_gate.py fixture and its eight fail-case tests, the test_commands_and_skills.py extensions) is still to be written at phase (c), so the 'code the existing tests already cover' condition for routine does not hold.
Tight spec is only one of the three routine conditions; the other two (small blast radius, existing coverage) still fail, so the plan stays non-routine regardless of this round's fix.
attempted: Intent: re-checked the current spec.md/plan.md against intent.md's Proposed outcome field-by-field; the fix round only adds the eighth fail case and renumbers seven-to-eight everywhere, introducing no scope drift; the two carried-forward open questions (cross-project sharing, eval-case frontmatter) are still correctly left to their named owners.

Spec and plan: targeted re-check of the exact gap named in the delegation prompt. Confirmed 'two lesson files matching the glob' (or equivalent wording) now appears in all four of plan.md's enumerations -- the checks.py 'Files that change' bullet, Order of work step 2, Risk 2's mitigation list, and the Proof section's test_gate.py item -- plus spec.md's Design/Determinism bullet ('more than one match fails the check') and spec.md's Acceptance bullet. All five/six count references were bumped from seven to eight (Risk 1's 'up to eight reasons', Order of work step 2's 'eight fail cases'); grepped both files for a stray 'seven' and found none. Verified in the diff itself (diff-b.patch) that these are additions within the single new-file hunks for spec.md and plan.md, not edits that could have missed a sibling location -- all four plan.md occurrences and both spec.md occurrences are present and consistent with each other (same ordering, same case names) in the final file content.

Proof: no code exists yet (phase b is design-only); the diff is confined to changes/0003-.../{spec.md, plan.md, status.yaml, evidence/*}. No toolchain log is expected or claimed for this phase and none was cited for or against the diff. claude-b.json, claude-fix.json, gate-b.json, run-b.json and the prior adversarial-review-b.json are runner/gate records from earlier rounds at earlier HEADs; read for timeline context only, never cited as evidence about HEAD 31ca678.

Blast radius: confirmed the diff touches only the change folder (spec.md, plan.md, status.yaml, evidence/*); no file under .claude/**, this repository's own CLAUDE.md/REVIEW.md/sdlc.yaml, or any workflow template; status.yaml's phase/iteration fields are the change folder's own tracking data, not a guardrail file.

Policies: re-checked data-conventions rules 1 and 3 ('no risk_list item applies', 'no personal data') and coding-standards rule 4 (test-before-behavior) -- rule 4 is exactly what the prior round's gap concerned, and the plan now names a test for every behavior the spec states, including the one that was missing.

The tests: cross-checked spec.md's determinism bullet and Acceptance bullet against plan.md's four parallel test-case enumerations one more time, case by case (missing lesson, two lesson files matching the glob, missing a required frontmatter field, prompt.md or checks.yaml missing, failing index.py check, dangling supersedes, a supersedes target whose status did not move to retired, out-of-enum status) -- all eight now agree, in the same order, across every location that restates them. No other fail case or edge appears to be missing. Change_type is 'feature', not 'fix', so the pre-existing-test-weakening rule does not apply, and no test file is touched in this diff anyway (phase b writes no tests).
